reading.label: Reading Archive
reading.title: I am what I read
reading.summary: A personal archive for books, moods, notes, and the traces reading leaves behind.
reading.description: This is the central reading archive: the place for books, dates, quotes, first impressions, and the small evidence of how a text stayed with you.
includes: Book notes
Title, author, dates, quotes, reading mood, and quick response.
Reading traces
Questions, obsessions, and small details that keep returning after you finish.
Reading timeline
A chronological view of what you read and what themes occupied you then.
sample: quiet, fragmented, alert to city sounds
Close Reading Lab: opening sentence and movement through London

criticism.label: My fiction
criticism.title: Welcome to my silly world
criticism.summary: Characters, fragments, scenes, and the private logic of unfinished stories.
criticism.description: This is the writing room: playful, strange, unfinished, and full of fragments that may become characters, scenes, or entire worlds.
includes: Characters
Names, voices, contradictions, desires, and private histories.
Fragments
Loose scenes, images, opening lines, endings, and sentences that want a home.
World notes
Rules, places, atmospheres, and recurring objects.
sample: A house that remembers more than its owner does
Tender, suspicious, sometimes too dramatic on purpose
A blue cup that appears in every room

context.label: Reflection
context.title: Don't lie to me
context.summary: Close reading, sharper claims, uncomfortable questions, and honest criticism.
context.description: This is where the archive becomes more exacting. It asks whether an interpretation is honest, whether the evidence holds, and what the text is really doing.
includes: Close reading
Quote, image, syntax, rhythm, context, and claim.
Argument check
What the claim says, what supports it, and where it might be weak.
Theory notes
Terms, methods, and frameworks that clarify the reading.
sample: The room is not only private space; it is a test of who is allowed to think.
Woolf's rooms, Morrison's houses, inherited memory
Needs a clearer distinction between room and house

fiction.label: Extra
fiction.title: And more...
fiction.summary: Loose notes, side quests, experiments, and anything that does not fit neatly elsewhere.
fiction.description: This is the overflow drawer: extra thoughts, small experiments, lists, links, and future sections that are not ready to become their own room yet.
includes: Loose notes
Small thoughts, saved lines, links, and ideas to revisit later.
Experiments
Formats, visual ideas, interactive sketches, and possible future blocks.
Parking lot
Things that may become a full section later.
sample: A small page for favorite sentences
A map of books by emotional weather
Decide whether it belongs on Home or Extra

reading.label: 阅读档案
reading.title: 我即我所读
reading.summary: 保存书、心情、笔记，以及阅读留下的痕迹。
reading.description: 这里是核心阅读档案：书目、日期、摘录、第一印象，以及一本书如何留在你身上的证据。
includes: 书籍笔记
标题、作者、日期、摘录、阅读心情和快速回应。
阅读痕迹
读完后仍反复出现的问题、迷恋和细节。
sample: 《达洛维夫人》 / 弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫 / 1925
安静、碎片化、对城市声音很敏感

criticism.label: 我的小说
criticism.title: 欢迎来到我的荒唐世界
criticism.summary: 人物、片段、场景，以及未完成故事的私人逻辑。
criticism.description: 这里是写作房间：好玩、奇怪、未完成，充满可能变成人物、场景或完整世界的碎片。
includes: 人物
名字、声音、矛盾、欲望和私人历史。
片段
松散场景、意象、开头句、结尾和等待归处的句子。
sample: 一栋比主人记得更多的房子
温柔、多疑，有时故意过分戏剧化

context.label: 思考札记
context.title: 不要对我说谎
context.summary: 细读、更锋利的论点、不舒服的问题和诚实的批评。
context.description: 这里让档案变得更严格：解释是否诚实，证据是否站得住，文本到底在做什么。
includes: 阅读札记
引文、意象、句法、节奏、语境和论点。
论点检查
论点说了什么、证据在哪里、薄弱处是什么。
sample: 房间不只是私人空间，也测试谁被允许思考。
伍尔夫的房间、莫里森的房屋、继承的记忆

fiction.label: 其他
fiction.title: 还有更多……
fiction.summary: 松散笔记、支线任务、实验，以及暂时无处安放的东西。
fiction.description: 这里是溢出的抽屉：额外想法、小实验、清单、链接和还没准备好成为独立房间的未来 section。
includes: 松散笔记
小想法、保存的句子、链接和以后再看的东西。
实验
形式、视觉想法、互动草图和未来可能的 block。
sample: 做一个喜欢的句子页面
按情绪天气给书做地图
